decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type matchups against Incineroar—Thunderbolt looks neutral, but Shadow Ball is resisted since Dark resists Ghost.

Running the Thunderbolt damage calc with STAB and life orb, it lands around 116 out of 202 HP, roughly 57%, not a guaranteed KO. I'm also considering whether Make It Rain would be any better, but Steel is resisted by Fire so that's worse. Instead I'm weighing the danger of Incineroar countering with Flare Blitz, which hits Gholdengo's Steel typing for super-effective damage while Ghost is neutral against it.

Since Gholdengo's immune to status, Parting Shot and similar tricks don't matter here, and Fake Out isn't available this turn. I'm now considering pivoting to Garchomp instead, since its Ground typing resists Fire and its Earthquake would hit Incineroar for 2x super-effective damage with strong Attack, though switching costs a free hit from Incineroar on the turn in.

Weighing the math more carefully, if Gholdengo stays and fires Thunderbolt, Incineroar's return Flare Blitz looks like it could actually KO Gholdengo outright given the 2x Fire-vs-Steel multiplier and STAB, even accounting for recoil. Switching to Garchomp instead means it only takes a halved Flare Blitz, keeping it in much better shape to counterattack with Earthquake next turn.

Running that Earthquake, with STAB and the 2x Ground weakness on Incineroar, it comes out to roughly a KO on Incineroar's remaining HP, and since Garchomp outspeeds, it should get that hit in first — even factoring in a possible Parting Shot attack drop. That makes switching into Garchomp the clearly better line, preserving Gholdengo and setting up a probable KO on Incineroar.
